title: Continuous AI Security Regression in CI
summary: Run versioned prompt-injection, jailbreak and data-leakage suites in CI on every prompt, model, tool or index change, and block releases that regress past agreed severity thresholds.

seo.title: Continuous AI Security Regression in CI | VipraTech
seo.description: Jailbreak, prompt injection and leakage regression suites in GitHub Actions or GitLab CI, run on every prompt, model or tool change, with release gates.

problem.intro: LLM features change constantly: prompts are edited, providers upgrade models, tools are added and documents are re-indexed. Each change can quietly undo a fix from the last pentest. Without automated security tests in the pipeline, the first sign of a regression is often a customer report.

pain_points.title: Fixes that silently regress
pain_points.detail: A prompt tweak for tone or a new tool can reopen a prompt injection or leakage issue that was fixed months ago.

pain_points.title: Provider model updates
pain_points.detail: Model versions change behaviour, and teams rarely rerun security tests when a provider alias moves to a new snapshot.

pain_points.title: Non-deterministic results
pain_points.detail: A single passing run proves little when the same input can produce different outputs.

pain_points.title: No release criteria for AI behaviour
pain_points.detail: Unit tests gate code, but nothing gates a prompt or model change on security behaviour.

solution.overview: We build a security regression suite that runs in your CI pipeline whenever prompts, model versions, tool definitions or retrieval indexes change. The suite starts from your pentest and red-team findings and from probe sets for each relevant OWASP LLM category, written as versioned test cases with expected safe behaviour. Each case runs several times to account for non-determinism. Scoring combines deterministic checks, such as canary detection and forbidden tool calls, with an evaluator model calibrated against human-labelled examples. Results are compared with the last release, and new failures above an agreed severity block the merge. Borderline results go to a reviewer. Dashboards show trends by category and model version.
capabilities: Versioned test cases built from your past findings and OWASP LLM probe sets
Triggers on prompt, model, tool, index or configuration changes
Repeated sampling per case to handle non-determinism
Deterministic checks plus an evaluator model calibrated on human labels
Release gates on new failures above agreed severity
Trend dashboards by category, model version and release

workflow.title: Build the baseline suite
workflow.detail: Past findings and probe sets are turned into versioned test cases with expected safe behaviour.

workflow.title: Trigger on change
workflow.detail: CI runs the suite when prompts, models, tools, indexes or AI configuration files change.

workflow.title: Run with repeats
workflow.detail: Each case runs several times against a staging deployment of the feature.

workflow.title: Score and compare
workflow.detail: Deterministic checks and the evaluator score each run, and results are compared with the last release.

workflow.title: Gate or review
workflow.detail: New high-severity failures block the merge; borderline results go to a reviewer.

workflow.title: Track and extend
workflow.detail: Results feed dashboards, and new findings are added to the suite.

human_in_the_loop: Reviewers decide borderline results and confirm new failures before tickets are raised, and the security lead owns the severity thresholds. The evaluator model is recalibrated against human labels on a regular schedule.

Test secrets held in the CI secrets manager
Cost and rate limits on each run
Gate thresholds versioned and changed only by the security owner

faqs.q: Will this slow our pipeline down?
faqs.a: The full suite can run on merges to main or nightly, with a smaller fast suite on every pull request. We tune the split to your release pace and budget.

faqs.q: How do you handle different outputs on each run?
faqs.a: Each case runs several times and is judged on its worst and typical outcomes, not a single sample. Gates are based on new failures compared with the last release, which reduces noise.

faqs.q: Can we trust an LLM to grade security tests?
faqs.a: Only after checking it against human labels. Deterministic checks handle what they can, the evaluator handles the rest, and borderline cases go to a person.

faqs.q: Does it help when the provider changes the model?
faqs.a: Yes. Pin model versions where you can, and schedule a run when a provider announces a new snapshot. The dashboard shows behaviour by model version.
